svg.title: alan-factory architecture
svg.desc: What you set up once (your Mac, two GitHub accounts, Claude Code, two SonarCloud users, Copilot review) and two flows: the build flow from a chat through the brief, planning, a split into two pull requests, review, feedback-driven fix rounds, automatic merge and self-update deploy, and the read-only explore flow from a consultant chat through the brief to a report.
svg.text: Two ways in: Explore to research and think a question through, or Build to change the code. Alan's agent teams do the rest, unattended.
① What you set up once
./setup.sh walks you through each of these
runs every team in both flows below · queues jobs · passes typed handovers between teams · parks and asks you when blocked
changes your code · everything after Dispatch runs on its own at the default posture “autonomous”

g.text: You describe the change you want
in the web UI and talk it through
Summarize turns the chat into a
brief; you review and edit it, then
writes the plan, the acceptance clauses
and the test scenarios the PR will be
codes in its own git worktree, runs
every gate, opens its own PR
one per subtask, shown here for one
Every subtask’s PR goes through the same flow from here on:
review → fix rounds → merge → self-update → deploy_verify.
check the diff against the plan, CI
and Copilot, then post the review
on GitHub as the verifier bot
waits until gate is green, the review
is approved and every thread is
waits for green CI on main, pulls it
to your Mac, rebuilds the UI and
confirms the merged change is live
each round: implementation_fix pushes to the same PR, then verification reviews it again · capped at a few rounds · Alan escalates to you at the cap, or sooner if the loop stalls

svg.text: read-only · researches and reasons about your repo and the web, opens no PR
Posture “autonomous” merges without human review once gate is green; lower it to “propose” in the web UI to approve each merge yourself. SonarCloud is optional and never blocks a merge.
